chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Husayn ibn Uthman from Isma'il ibn Jabr said:
I requested permission from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while we were fasting in Ramadan to meet Walid at al-A'was, so he said, 'Go meet him and break your fast.'

key_terms.بِالْأَعْوَصِ: At al-A'was, a location near Mecca
key_terms.رَمَضَانَ: The month of fasting in the Islamic calendar
key_terms.وَلِيداً: A specific person, Walid ibn Abi Umayyah or another companion, mentioned by name

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on breaking the fast in Ramadan when one needs to go out to meet someone?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) instructs Isma'il ibn Jabir to break his fast while traveling to meet Walid ibn Abi al-Mughira at al-A'was, highlighting the flexibility of fasting rules for those engaged in necessary travel or duties. This ruling underscores the principle that the ease (*rukhas*) granted to travelers extends to specific needs encountered during the journey, rather than requiring the completion of the fast before attending to such matters. The context reflects the practical application of *fiqh* in social and political interactions during the early Islamic period.
